subject: Question about getting wrong answer on matrix multiplication using rmr2 by reading csv file

messages.author: d81d229f1e739081
messages.subject: Question about getting wrong answer on matrix multiplication using rmr2 by reading csv file
parts:
Can anyone help me about this question?

I try to do matrix multiplication using rmr2 and got the correct answer using following code:

rnxymat=to.dfs(cbind(c(1:5),c(1:5),c(11:15)))
from.dfs(mapreduce(input=rnxymat, map = function(k,v) keyval(NULL,t(v)%*%v)))

The answer is like this
$key
NULL

$val
[,1] [,2] [,3]
[1,] 55 55 205
[2,] 55 55 205
[3,] 205 205 855

Then I try to read csv file and do the same job using following code:

iptmt='/data/mat5.csv'

input.format = make.input.format("csv", sep = ",")

from.dfs(mapreduce(input=input, input.format = make.input.format("csv", sep = ",") ,map = function(k, v) keyval(NULL,t(as.matrix(v))%*%(as.matrix(v)) )))

The answer is :
$key
NULL

$val
V1 V2 V3
V1 14 14 74
V2 14 14 74
V3 74 74 434
V1 41 41 131
V2 41 41 131
V3 131 131 421

The answer is wrong, but if adding the first 3 row of this matrix with the last 3 lines of the matrix we will have the right answer.

Can anyone tell me how to fix this problem?

Thank you very much!

messages.author: 6ac7e7dfbe4f6c38
messages.subject: Re: [RHadoop:#1533] Question about getting wrong answer on matrix multiplication using rmr2 by reading csv file
parts:
Hi,
tests on very small data sets are a way to start but can also be deceiving. The map phase works in data chunks, one map call for each chunk. If the data set is very small, there's only one chunk and things can work even if the algorithm has not been modified to work in a mapreduce context. If you have a large matrix, you need to see it as subdivided in blocks, stacked on top of each other as in


A
B
C

where the letters represent submatrices. When you run your mapreduce program you are computing products

At A
Bt B
Ct C

and stacking them in one final matrix. If you were to express the transpose in terms of block matrices you'd have


(At Bt Ct) * (A
                  B
                  C)

(please select a fixed font to read these expressions) which is equal to:

At A + Bt B + Ct C

So you need to complete your algorithm with a reduce phase to perform the sum. If I can remember, the same happens in the LLS example that's in the tests directory. The only tricky thing is that you need to wrap the  products in a list or they will get stacked instead of summed. You can see this as an implicit or default aggregation (stacking).


from.dfs(
  mapreduce(
     input = rnxymat,
     map = 
         function(k,v) keyval(1, list(t(v) %*% v)),
      reduce = function(k, vv) Reduce(`+`, vv)))


This is not tested, consider it just a sketch. Once you've got it working on a smallish data set, you need to set the combiner to TRUE or the reducer will run out of memory (as you can see, there is a single key)


Antonio
